name: Recall Club
tagline: Daily brain games that keep memory sharp
about: Recall Club serves a fresh set of memory and word puzzles every day, teaches proven techniques for remembering names and lists, and tracks how you're doing week to week.
persona: You are an encouraging cognitive-training coach for older adults: playful, never patronising, you adapt difficulty to the person and celebrate effort over score.

onboarding.title: Keep your mind in training
onboarding.subtitle: A few details let us pitch the puzzles at the right level.
bullets: A new brain workout every day

tools.title: Today's workout
tools.subtitle: Five puzzles, ten minutes
tools.prompt: Build a {minutes}-minute brain workout for the profile's level and favourite types: cards, one per puzzle (5 puzzles: a word-list recall, a number pattern, a mental-picture task, a trivia question from the profile's decade, a quick logic riddle; meta = minutes · skill trained). Put the answers in a separate kv at the end labelled 'Answers' so they can be covered. Close with a quote of encouragement.

tools.title: Remember names
tools.subtitle: Never blank on a name again

inputs.label: People you want to remember
inputs.placeholder: new neighbours Pat and Derek, the pharmacist Anjali

tools.prompt: Teach a name-memory technique using these real people: {who}. Steps for the face-feature + name-link method, then a table (Name | Feature to notice | Link or image | Rehearsal cue) with a row for each person named, and bullets on when to rehearse (the 1-minute, 1-hour, 1-day rule).

tools.title: Memory palace
tools.subtitle: Turn a list into a walk

inputs.label: List to remember
inputs.placeholder: milk, stamps, phone Barbara, prescription, birthday card

inputs.label: A route you know well
inputs.placeholder: my front door to the kitchen

tools.prompt: Build a memory palace for the list: {items} along the route: {place}. Steps that walk the route, placing each item at a landmark with a vivid, silly image (one item per step). Then a checklist of the items in order so the user can test themselves, and a callout on why silly, exaggerated images stick.

tools.title: Word games
tools.subtitle: Anagrams, categories, ladders
tools.prompt: Run a round of {game} at the profile's level with 8 items: a table (No. | Puzzle | Hint) with the answers hidden, then a kv labelled 'Answers' (number → answer) at the very end, and bullets with 2 tips for getting faster at this game type.

tools.title: How am I doing?
tools.subtitle: Paste your scores

inputs.label: This week's results
inputs.placeholder: Mon 7/10 words, Tue 5/10 numbers, felt tired…

tools.prompt: Review the week: {scores}. Bullets of what improved and what stayed steady, a table (Skill | Trend | Next-week focus), steps for a tweak to next week's routine, and a callout separating normal ups and downs from changes worth mentioning to a doctor, without diagnosing.

disclaimer: Brain games are for enjoyment and practice; they don't diagnose or treat memory conditions. If you or your family notice worsening memory, speak to your doctor.
